item.title: Pennsylvania teacher preserved his white pumpkin for nearly 40 years; gardeners now grow it too
item.description: Wayne Fortna, a Pennsylvania teacher, preserved a unique cream-colored pumpkin variety for decades. He found solace in gardening after serving as a tank commander during World War II. His daughter helped save the heirloom seeds through a local museum after his passing. The Landis Valley Village and Farm Museum maintained the precious seeds for future generations. Seed Savers Exchange now shares these special pumpkin seeds with gardeners worldwide.

item.title: A developer planned to bulldoze this 1910 Oregon bungalow and divide its 1.04-acre lot
item.description: In a remarkable turn of events, a historic Arts and Crafts bungalow from 1910 was spared from demolition by developers. The property underwent a meticulous restoration that lasted several years, ensuring modern systems were integrated while retaining its classic charm. Ultimately, this stunning 3,074-square-foot residence was sold for an impressive $1.47 million, preserving a vital chapter of local history.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2001, Arthur Blank bought his first Montana guest ranch; 25 years later, his four properties span...
item.description: Arthur Blank is enhancing his business footprint in Montana with the introduction of Auster at Dome Mountain, a stunning riverfront lodge situated by the Yellowstone River. After acquiring this historic site in December 2021, he meticulously redeveloped it to include accessible dining and retail spaces for the public, furthering his longstanding dedication to conservation within the picturesque Paradise Valley.

item.title: In 1979, Beach Boys co-founder Mike Love paid $435,000 for a 2.5-acre Lake Tahoe property
item.description: Mike Love, the iconic singer of the Beach Boys, has put his stunning Lake Tahoe estate on the market for an impressive forty-three million dollars. This beautiful property has been cherished by his family for over 40 years. Originally purchased as undeveloped land, this expansive estate now showcases breathtaking lake and mountain views, providing a serene retreat.

item.title: 31-year-old California entrepreneur builds $4.3 million portable-toilet business
item.description: Daniel Tom, 31, started Bay Area Sanitation in California in 2023 with one truck and 100 portable toilets. The business became profitable within its first year and generated $4.3 million in 2025. It now operates nearly 2,000 toilets and 12 trucks, with Tom focusing on long-term rentals, regular cleaning and reinvesting profits to expand the company further.

item.title: California approves $5 mn toward Chumash Tribe’s $18 mn purchase of former abalone farm land
item.description: California has approved $5 million towards the purchase of 357 coastal acres in Cayucos that once housed the largest abalone farm in the US. The yak titʸu titʸu yak tiłhini Northern Chumash Tribe is raising $18 million to buy the property, restore native habitats, revive aquaculture and support research into endangered white and black abalone.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Drake Maye, wife pay $15,000 classroom costs for 54 Providence school educators
item.description: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and his wife, Ann Michael, paid for the classroom wish lists of all 54 teachers and support specialists at Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School in Providence, Rhode Island. The $15,000 donation through their MayeDay Family Foundation came as 98% of the school’s students receive free or reduced-price lunch.

item.title: In 2006, a Rhode Island man bought a Florida lot; 18 years later, North Port banned new homes, he sued
item.description: A Florida city has made a zoning change that blocks a resident from constructing his much-anticipated retirement home. After acquiring the lot nearly two decades ago with plans for development, he now faces obstacles due to new city regulations aimed at boosting commercial growth. The legal challenge claims these changes infringe upon his constitutional rights, showcasing the significant effects of zoning laws on property owners' expectations.

item.title: In 2019, Wisconsin turned 87,000 cubic yards of harbor dredge into 14 acres of shorebird habitat
item.description: After nearly five decades, piping plovers triumphantly return to Wisconsin Point, symbolizing a remarkable achievement in conservation. Thanks to a dedicated $4.5 million habitat restoration initiative, 14 acres of essential nesting and feeding grounds have been established from harbor sediment. Protective measures like seasonal closures and predator exclosures have been implemented to ensure the safety of these delicate birds.

item.title: "Coolest thing any streamer does": Jynxzi steps outside gaming to support Maya Higa’s wildlife mission with $100,000 donation
item.description: Renowned streamer Jynxzi has generously contributed $100,000 to Alveus Sanctuary, a nonprofit aimed at wildlife conservation led by Maya Higa. This remarkable donation will aid in providing homes for various animals and enhancing educational outreach about wildlife. Jynxzi expressed deep respect for Higa's commitment to conservation, demonstrating a powerful impact that online influencers can make on animal welfare initiatives.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Google, Bill Gates's fund invests $31.8M in California startup aiming to build solar farm using robots
item.description: A California startup has successfully garnered considerable funding to enhance its robotic technology for solar park installations. Planted seeks to redefine the construction industry by creating a repeatable, production-line method. By employing advanced software and robotics, they precisely position solar panel posts, allowing for installations across diverse terrains and maximizing energy productivity per acre. Their groundbreaking approach is set to hasten the adoption of solar energy on a larger scale.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who is Joe Petraro-Hyppolite the 13-year-old boy with 168 IQ?
item.description: At just 13, Joe Petraro-Hyppolite from Long Island is defying age expectations as he embarks on a master's program at New York University. He notably graduated high school at 11 and scored an impressive 1590 on the SAT by age 10. Joe is diving into disciplines such as sports management, kinesiology, and biology, aiming to complete his undergraduate degree next Spring, solidifying his place among exceptional academic achievers.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: California approves $42M to protect Wild Cherry Canyon
item.description: California has taken a major step in environmental conservation by approving a new grant for the Wild Cherry Canyon project. Spanning 2,060 acres, this coastal area will be safeguarded from any development and transformed into a nature preserve. With a focus on habitat restoration and community engagement, tribal communities will partner in maintaining this valuable ecological site, welcoming visitors to enjoy its natural beauty.
